documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy (AI-001)
documents.summary: UTRGV's AI-001 is an institution-wide governance policy for developing, buying and deploying AI systems, with principles, risk assessment, inventory and training duties. It says almost nothing about student use of AI in coursework or academic integrity.
documents.stance_why: Coder A coded delegates and coder B permit. The policy never hands the decision to instructors or courses; it says UTRGV "encourages education and research in AI" and "fosters innovation", and it allows AI use under conditions: AI-generated content must be "independently verified", controlled data "may only be used with approved AI tools", and every tool must "pass the necessary IT and ISO technology assessment". It bans only "Discriminatory, biased, malicious, or harmful use of AI". That is permission with conditions, so permit. It does not address coursework, so this is a stance on AI use in general, not on student work.

documents.summary: The Center for Teaching Excellence offers three optional model syllabus statements on generative AI: exploratory, permitted as specified, and no use. Instructors choose and adapt one.
documents.stance_why: Both coders coded delegates and listed the three sample statements. The page offers them as "only an example and optional" and says "Please modify as you see fit", so the instructor chooses; the stance is delegates with tiers.

units.why: The statements are "only an example and optional": the CTE does not set a university rule and leaves syllabus choices to instructors. P04.
units.anchor: These potential approaches are only an example and optional in case you would like to

units.why: "Please modify as you see fit" lets instructors change the sample wording; leaving the choice of AI wording to the instructor is P04, instructor, before-course, may.
units.anchor: Please modify as you see fit and align to your teaching values, beliefs, and course
units.resolution_why: Modality and type differed (A may P04, B should P83) because the sentence holds two directions. "Modify as you see fit" is permission to adapt (P04, may); "align to your teaching values, beliefs, and course learning objectives" is coded as its own unit (P83, should).

units.why: "align to your teaching values, beliefs, and course learning objectives" asks instructors to base their AI approach on learning objectives, so P83, instructor, before-course, should.
units.anchor: align to your teaching values, beliefs, and course learning objectives
units.policy: Please modify as you see fit and align to your teaching values, beliefs, and course learning objectives.
units.resolution_why: Coder B coded this half of the sentence (P83, should); coder A coded the whole sentence as P04. The alignment direction is a different rule from "modify as you see fit", so it is kept as its own unit.

units.why: Offers three named options (exploratory, permitted, no use); a menu of tiers, P05.
units.anchor: Use of Generative AI as Exploratory Potential
units.policy: The CTE offers three suggested syllabus approaches to generative AI: exploratory, permitted as specified by the instructor, and no use.
units.resolution_why: Phase differed (A course-start, B before-course). The page offers instructors three samples to pick from when designing their syllabus, which is policy design, so before-course.

units.why: Statement 1 sample text: the instructor "intend[s] to embed" AI in the course. It builds AI into coursework: P79.
units.anchor: I intend to embed the use of them in my course
units.resolution_why: unit_stance differed (A require, B encourage). The sample statement says "I intend to embed the use of them in my course", so AI is built into the work, which is the require definition. Modality informs because it is a sample sentence an instructor may adopt.

units.why: Statement 1 invites students to "share your feedback" while exploring AI together with the instructor, engaging students in discussing the AI approach (P66).

units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. "Join me on this exploratory journey and share your feedback" is part of sample Statement 1 and invites students to take part; it is a weak but real statement about how the course treats AI, so kept.

units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. "Generative AI chatbots offer valuable benefits if approached responsibly and ethically" is a statement of the benefit of AI in sample Statement 2, so kept.

notes: Only the three university-layer documents were coded; school and computing units were not found and course is deferred. AI-001 is mostly governance of AI development, procurement and deployment, so most of its units are P65, P80, P98 and P77 and few concern student coursework. The three syllabus statements on the CTE page are optional sample wording, so units quoting them describe what the template says, not a binding rule. Fit notes and uncovered notes from both coders were kept (loose fits: P80, P103, P88, P52, P65). Neither coder proposed new types. The document stance for AI-001 was a disagreement (A delegates, B permit) resolved to permit; see stance_why.
